To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed and validated a molecular classifier of MYc activity using formalin-fixed,paraffin-embedded (FFPE) biopsy specimens, that the classifier accurately predicts survival among patients with primary diffuse large B-cell (DLBCL), and that the classifier can be used to subclassify B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable,with features intermediate between BLand DLBCL (BL-U), as molecular BL or molecular DLBCL.

we developed a diagnostic molecular classifier for MYC-driven, B-cell lymphoma using RNA from fixed tissue specimens, and that the classifier accurately predicted pathological diagnosis, molecular subclassification, and stratified patients according to MYC activity.

the development of molecular diagnostic tests for the classification of B-cell lymphoma and the stratification of patients with aggressive B-cell lymphoma for risk-adapted treatment.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the molecular classifier accurately predicted the pathological diagnosis of BL and DLBC, and provided more accurate subclassification for a group of BCL-U cases as molecular BL or molecular DLBC, and also stratified DLBC patients with MYC activity into high- and intermediate- or low-risk groups.

a targeted expression profiling assay accurately classified B-cell lymphomas as BL and DLBLCL, and resolved the heterogeneity of B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable with features intermediate between Burkitt lymphoma and diffuse large B cell lymphoma, into molecular Burkitt lymphoma, molecular diffuse large B cell, and a small number of genetic double-hit lymphoma cases.
the molecular classification is not a replacement of the histological classification but rather an extension of the current classification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown the feasibility of a targeted gene expression profiling panel to categorize tumors into BL and DLBLC and resolve the molecular heterogeneities of BCL-U as molecular BL or molecular DLBCL and that a MYC activity classifier correlated with MYC immunohistochemistry and stratified patients into high and low risk groups.
the molecular classification of MYC driven B cell lymphomas can be done with a targeted expression profiling.

the molecular profiling of fixed tissue specimens can be used to categorically classify B-cell lymphomas as BL, DLBCL, or BCL-U, to resolve the heterogeneity of B-cell lymphoma with MYC translocation, and to predict outcome in patients with primary DLCL treated with R-Chop.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a new diagnostic test to help classify B-cell lymphomas.
we developed an assay that can classify B-cell lymphomas as Burkitt, diffuse large B-cell, or unclassifiable and can also predict the activity of MYC in a lymphoma.

a small set of targeted genes, selected on the basis of biological knowledge, can be used to accurately classify and stratify aggressive B-cell lymphomas using RNA from formal-fixed, paraffined-embedded biopsy specimens, which can be obtained from the clinical files of most institutions.
